q1_issues.issue: "not necessarily" is flattened into a plain strength-0.0 denial, which asserts that the magazine does not glorify the Bush administration — a stronger claim than the text, which denies only that it must.
The denial carries confidence 0.9 while its positive twin carries 0.99, with nothing in the confidence dial licensing the drop for an individual fact.
The explicit adversative "but" gets no connective atom, although both conjuncts are reified as eventualities and But is a licensed surface connective head.

q2_gaps: "not necessarily" — a negation scoping over an epistemic necessity modal (not-must-P rather than must-not-P) has no licensed carrier

an eponymous capitalized modifier naming a DIFFERENT entity the head noun is associated with ("the Bush administration") — the naming template ("the Brindle estuary") assumes the capitalized run names the referent itself, which here would wrongly give (Member bush administration)
elliptical NP-coordination under "but not ..." — the connective section assumes two full clauses, so it is unclear whether the reconstructed VP counts as an endpoint
notes: The denial correctly reconstructs the elided verb and correctly projects the definite "the Bush administration" outside the strength-0 bundle, and Theme on glorify / put and Location on the positioning event are all right. The parse routes that NP through Possession, which the genitive rule licenses only for 's, a possessive pronoun, or an of-phrase — not for a bare capitalized modifier.
